subject.title: Add external event hooks for quota and provider state changes

question: Should CodexBar permanently support user-configured commands launched from background quota/provider events through shared config and the app UI?
rationale: The patch is deliberately hardened and opt-in, but it still changes CodexBar from observation-only behavior to a persistent local code-execution trigger and establishes a compatibility-sensitive automation API; source review cannot infer whether that boundary belongs in the product.

options.title: Accept hardened hooks
options.body: Approve the opt-in direct-exec boundary after the argv editor preserves the exact structured argument array and focused regression coverage passes.

options.title: Narrow the surface
options.body: Limit hooks to config/CLI management or a smaller event set before accepting background execution in the GUI app.

options.title: Decline local execution
options.body: Keep CodexBar observation-only and close the PR and paired feature request without adding command hooks.

recommendation.title: Accept hardened hooks
recommendation.body: Approve the opt-in direct-exec boundary after the argv editor preserves the exact structured argument array and focused regression coverage passes.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner is the clearest available decision owner for a new product-wide local execution and long-lived configuration contract.
